title: Squeezing-Fueled Quantum Otto Engine via Measurement-Induced Cooling: The Two-Qubit Quantum Rabi Model
abstract: We investigate a quantum Otto engine (QOE) constructed from the two-qubit quantum Rabi model, operating within a cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED) architecture. The engine operates with two qubits as the working substance and a single non-Markovian hot thermal bath, modeled via the hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) formalism. In place of a conventional cold thermal reservoir, the cooling stroke is realized through a projective measurement protocol on the cavity mode, which acts as an ancillary subsystem and effectively mimics a cold bath for the qubit working medium via measurement back-action. A squeezing drive applied to the cavity mode serves as a quantum fuel. We demonstrate that cavity squeezing systematically enhances both the power output and operational efficiency of the engine - the work extracted per unit of heat drawn from the hot bath-driving it above the standard quantum Otto limit. In the limit-cycle regime, the efficiency, while remaining above the Otto bound throughout, asymptotically converges to it from above. This identifies squeezing as a controllable quantum resource for thermodynamic optimization. Our results reveal that the interplay between qubit-cavity coupling, measurement-induced cooling, and non-equilibrium squeezing gives rise to a multi-resource thermodynamic architecture with performance characteristics inaccessible to conventional two-bath quantum Otto engines, thereby providing a concrete route toward experimentally realizable quantum heat engines in cavity QED platforms.
summary: The paper analyzes a Quantum Otto Engine built from two qubits coupled to a cavity mode, utilizing measurement-induced cooling instead of a traditional cold bath. By applying squeezing as an external fuel, the authors demonstrate that both power and efficiency are enhanced beyond established limits, establishing a blueprint for advanced quantum heat engines in QED systems.
main_problem: Investigating how quantum resources like squeezing and measurement back-action can enhance the performance of a Quantum Otto Engine (QOE) beyond standard thermodynamic limits.
main_result: Squeezing systematically enhances both the power output and operational efficiency, allowing the engine to operate above the standard quantum Otto limit by utilizing non-classical correlations.
method: The analysis combines theoretical modeling using the Hierarchical Equations of Motion (HEOM) for bath interactions with perturbative treatments of squeezing effects on work extraction and heat absorption across the four thermodynamic strokes.
model_or_system: The system is a two-qubit working substance coupled to a cavity mode, operating within a Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics (QED) architecture. The engine cycle is driven by non-Markovian hot baths and cooled via projective measurement on the cavity mode.
key_observables: Power output, operational efficiency ($\eta$), coherence ($\zeta(t)$), entanglement, and work extracted ($W$).
important_parameters: Squeezing strength ($\mu$ or $r$), squeezing phase ($\phi$), bath temperature, and coupling constants ($g_1, g_2$).
main_assumptions: The cold stroke is modeled by projective measurement back-action rather than thermal contact; the analysis confines itself to a specific invariant subspace (Sector A).
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the Quantum Otto cycle dynamics involving two coupled qubits interacting with a common cavity.
paper_structure: The paper details the Hamiltonian and system decomposition, applies HEOM for bath interactions, analyzes work extraction during non-adiabatic strokes using squeezing terms, calculates heat absorption modified by coherence, and finally formulates the total resource-inclusive efficiency ($\eta_{	ext{tot}}$).
why_interesting: This work directly addresses quantum thermodynamics in a highly relevant platform (Cavity QED), showing how engineered quantum resources can overcome fundamental thermodynamic bounds.
